verdict: The algebra of sections 3.3-3.8 holds as specified. The statement (c0_i = r_i·B for all i; c_i − c_1 = r_i·A_i − r_1·A_1 for i ≥ 2) is sufficient: any witness vector gives c_i − r_i·A_i = c_1 − r_1·A_1 =: M for every i, and an honest recipient's a_i·c0_i equals r_i·A_i exactly because c0_i is forced into the prime-order subgroup, so dalek's reduced-mod-ℓ signing scalar and the unreduced clamped scalar agree. Special soundness with one challenge and n responses extracts a single r_i = (s_i − s_i')/(e − e') per index that satisfies both the T_i and the V_i relation simultaneously, so no prover can pass with two different M values. The transcript carries everything the verifier depends on (group_id, dek_commit, n, every A_i/c0_i/c_i in sorted order, commitments); the DDH hybrid goes through for A' = A_v + t·B, A' = t·A_v, sums and negations because each wrap's masking term r_i·A_i uses independent randomness; small-order/identity keys and every point any party multiplies (A_i, c0_i, c_i, signature R) are rejected or exactly checked; verify_strict plus author ∈ G removes signature malleability so hashing body‖sig is safe; and the epoch-sig prefix cannot collide with any message iroh 1.0.3 signs with the same key (verified in the pinned sources: rustls CertificateVerify starts with 64 × 0x20; iroh-relay signs a 32-byte blake3::derive_key output or a TLS-exporter value, both shorter than any epoch message; pkarr signing lives in iroh-dns and signs client-built records). No critical finding. One major: the keyless randomness/M-reuse detection (D10/R5) is narrower than the leak it targets (within-record, cross-group, and m = r_i degeneracies). The remaining findings are precision fixes to the security argument (public-discrete-log M is not DoS), S5/cache semantics for non-rotating records, transcript/carry wording, version-trap and iroh-signing text, seed-copy hygiene, and the whole-chain state assumption behind R2/R5 that a pin-only client verifier cannot meet. findings.title: R5's per-group, 'seen earlier' scope does not cover the randomness-reuse cases that actually publish M
findings.detail: D10 claims that remembering seen c0 and dek_commit values 'makes randomness reuse and M reuse detectable without a key'. Three concrete cases fall outside R5 as written ('no c0_i equals any c0 seen EARLIER in the chain', sets kept PER GROUP): (1) Within one record. 3.3 draws m and every r_i from the same OsRng pattern (from_bytes_mod_order_wide of 64 fresh bytes). If the RNG repeats inside one wrap set, m = r_1 = … = r_n, so M = m·B = c0_i: the record literally publishes M as every c0_i, every verifier accepts (all c0 are new to the chain), and anyone with the record computes DEK = KDF(c0_1, group_id). Even without m = r, equal r_i = r_j inside a record with a related registered key (A_j = −A_i, D1) gives c_i + c_j = 2M, i.e. the exact attack D1 was chosen to close. (2) Across groups. The backup key and (mode A) the authority are recipients of every group, so an r reused across two groups' records by the same client yields c_auth^(1) − c_auth^(2) = M_1 − M_2, computable from the two records by anyone; a reader of group 1 who can see group 2's chain (stolen SQLite, or a replica of group 1 that is not a reader of group 2) learns group 2's M. Per-group c0 sets never compare these. (3) M reuse across groups is invisible to the commit set because dek_commit is salted with group_id (3.4): identical M in two groups yields two different commits, yet a reader of one group derives the other's DEK as KDF(M, group_id_2). The spec hedges k_i against RNG repetition (3.5) but not r_i, although r_i repetition is the failure that discloses M rather than merely a nonce.
findings.fix: Make R5 explicit that c0 values must be pairwise distinct within the record as well as against the chain; add the keyless check KDF(c0_i, group_id) ≠ dek_commit for every i (catches m = r_i for one HKDF per wrap); keep the seen-c0 set bunker-wide on the server (same few KB per epoch; it is where R5 is enforced at submission), with replicas keeping it per group they mirror; and hedge r_i as from_bytes_mod_order_wide(SHA-512('secret-bunker-iroh/r/1' ‖ 0x00 ‖ m_or_M_bytes ‖ A_i ‖ u32be(i) ‖ OsRng 64)) so that with a stuck RNG a rotate gives pairwise-distinct r_i ≠ m, and a rewrap with the same M and recipient set reproduces old c0 values and is refused by R5 instead of leaking. Reword D10 to state the residual: relations between r values chosen by a colluding author are not detectable and are not in scope.

findings.title: The commit check that protects readers is only stated for rotating records, and the (group_id, dek_commit) DEK cache masks a bad rewrap at the server
findings.detail: The proof binds the wraps to each other, not to dek_commit; only 3.6 step 5 (a recipient opening its wrap) binds them to the committed key. S5 is written as a rotation flow ('decrypts every staged row under the new DEK … decrypts the row it replaces under the old DEK'), and 6.2 says a rewrap has 'no re-encryption, no stage'. S8 caches the DEK per (group_id, dek_commit). Concrete scenario: an admin authors a rewrap adding reader Y in which every wrap opens to a random M* while dek_commit equals head.dek_commit (required by R2). E/C/R/A/G pass, R3's proof passes (it is honest for M*). If the server does not open its own wrap for a non-rotating record, the record is installed; the server keeps serving plaintext from the cached DEK for the unchanged commit, so nothing fails at the authoritative node, while every replica (P4), the new reader Y, and every admin opening 'own wrap in head' (6.1 step 2) get M* and fail closed. The server itself discovers the problem only at restart, when the cache is empty and the head's authority wrap opens to M*. S5's stated purpose ('an admin cannot brick a group with garbage') is then not met for rewrap/recovery-without-rotate, and the cache key by dek_commit is exactly what hides it.
findings.fix: State S5's first clause unconditionally: for every mode-A record that carries wraps (rewrap, rotate, recovery in either branch) the server opens its own wrap from THAT record and refuses unless KDF(M') commit equals dek_commit; only the staged-row clauses are rotation-specific. Populate the DEK cache only from a wrap opened for the head being installed (key it by head hash, or re-derive on every head change), never by commit lookup alone. Add 'rewrap whose wraps open to a different M' to the S5 negative matrix in section 13.

findings.title: A committed M with a public discrete log is a silent key publication, not the denial of service the argument describes
findings.detail: 3.8 says the only unproven thing about M is that 'a malicious author can commit to garbage — a detectable, attributable denial of service'. But an author may choose M = t·B for a t it publishes (or M = B, 2B, …), compute dek_commit honestly, and produce honest wraps and a valid proof. Every reader's step-5 check passes, S5 passes, replicas accept, and the group's DEK is KDF(t·B, group_id) for anyone who knows t, from the record alone. Only the identity point is excluded (3.8 'the identity publishes M verbatim'); M = B is one addition away and is not excluded by any rule. This is equivalent in power to an admin leaking the DEK out of band, so it is not a new capability, but it is not DoS and it is not 'caught at step 5 of 3.6 or at the AEAD tag'. Separately, the same list says 'that the author knows M' is not proven, whereas the PoK of r_1 together with c_1 gives M = c_1 − r_1·A_1, so knowledge of M by the prover IS implied.
findings.fix: Rewrite the paragraph: the proof and commit check guarantee consistency of what recipients receive, not confidentiality against the author; an author can publish M (M = t·B with t disclosed) and this is indistinguishable from an honest rotation, which is why authorship is restricted to admins who can read anyway. Optionally reject the trivially checkable commits KDF(O), KDF(B) and KDF(c0_i) (see the R5 finding) so the degenerate cases are loud. Drop 'that the author knows M' from the not-proven list.

findings.title: The transcript omits epoch/prev on a rationale the carry rule does not actually use
findings.detail: 3.5 justifies leaving epoch, prev, acl and author out of the transcript because a transplantable wrap set 'is exactly what a carry record relies on'. R4 says a carry has n_s = 0 and proof_e = 0^32 and is accepted because every wrap entry is byte-identical to head.wraps — the proof is never re-verified for a carry, so proof transplantability buys the carry nothing. The consequence of the omission is that a valid proof is bound only to (group_id, dek_commit), and the spec then needs R5 (fresh c0 per non-carry record, with full-chain state) to forbid re-use of an old wrap set plus proof at another chain position by the same author. Binding the position into the transcript would make that class of replay fail the proof itself, independent of the seen-c0 state.
findings.fix: Add prev (32) and u64be(epoch) — or simply the head hash — to T after dek_commit, and correct the sentence in 3.5: carry relies on byte-identity of the wraps (R4), not on the proof; the proof is position-bound and R5 remains only as the randomness-reuse detector.

findings.title: Version-trap and iroh-signing statements do not match the pinned crates
findings.detail: 3.1 says curve25519-dalek 5 binds Scalar::random/from_hash/hash_to_curve to rand_core 0.9. The pinned curve25519-dalek 5.0.0 (Cargo.lock) depends on rand_core 0.10 and digest 0.11; ed25519-dalek 3.0.0 pulls sha2 0.11 and rand_core 0.10, while the project pins rand 0.8 (rand_core 0.6) and sha2 0.10, so the workaround (from_bytes_mod_order_wide fed by rand 0.8 OsRng / sha2 0.10) is right but the stated reason is not what was 'verified against the pinned crates'. 3.7 says 'Pure Ed25519 with a prefix is what iroh::SecretKey::sign … already do': iroh-base 1.0.3 SecretKey::sign is plain SigningKey::sign(msg) with no prefix; the domain separation in iroh's own uses comes from the callers (rustls builds the 64 × 0x20 CertificateVerify content; iroh-relay signs blake3::derive_key('iroh-relay handshake v1 challenge signature', challenge) or a TLS-exporter value), and pkarr signing lives in iroh-dns via iroh::address_lookup::pkarr, not a pkarr crate. The separation conclusion is still correct (all those messages are fixed-length and shorter than any epoch message, or start with 0x20), but the sentence as written would mislead the Go implementer into expecting iroh to add a prefix.
findings.fix: Correct 3.1 to rand_core 0.10 / digest 0.11 / sha2 0.11 for dalek 5 and ed25519-dalek 3. Rewrite the 3.7 sentence: iroh signs raw messages; the epoch prefix is added by this code, and every other message the key signs in iroh 1.0.3 is either a TLS 1.3 CertificateVerify (64 × 0x20 prefix), a 32-byte blake3-derived relay challenge, a TLS-exporter value, or an iroh-dns/pkarr BEP44 record ('3:seq…'). Pin those facts with a test that the signed epoch message is never 32 or 64 bytes long and never starts with 0x20.

findings.title: Seed copy from SecretKey::to_bytes is not in the zeroization list
findings.detail: 3.1/3.2 build the ElGamal scalar as SigningKey::from_bytes(&seed).to_scalar() from 'the iroh secret key bytes'. iroh::SecretKey::to_bytes() returns a fresh [u8; 32] seed copy on the stack; the existing agebridge::identity_from_secret does the same and never scrubs it. The hygiene list names r_i, k_i, m, M, a, DEK and the 64-byte buffers, but not this seed copy nor the ExpandedSecretKey produced inside to_scalar() (which is ZeroizeOnDrop, fine) — the seed array is the one that outlives its use unscrubbed on every decryption.
findings.fix: Use iroh_base SecretKey::as_signing_key() (present in iroh-base 1.0.3, returns &SigningKey) and call to_scalar() on it, so no seed copy is made; if a copy is unavoidable, wrap it in Zeroizing<[u8; 32]> and add it to the hygiene list.

findings.title: R2/R5 need whole-chain state, but the client-side verifier in 6.1 holds only a pin
findings.detail: 3.6 step 1 requires a reader to have 'fully verified (section 5)' a record before opening it, and R2 ('dek_commit differs from every commit seen in the chain') and R5 ('no c0_i equals any c0 seen earlier in the chain') are defined over the whole chain, with the sets 'derived from stored records on startup'. 6.1 step 1 has the admin client fetch GroupEpochs{since: pinned head} and 'verify the tail against the local pin'; 'peak client memory is one page' and no client-side record store is specified. A pin-only verifier cannot evaluate R2's history clause or R5 on the tail, so either the client silently skips two normative rules before opening its wrap (contradicting 3.6 step 1), or it must refetch from genesis on every operation. The same applies to the offline recovery author (6.4) unless the bundle is guaranteed to contain the full chain.
findings.fix: State the verifier-state contract: a verifier that does not hold the full chain must fetch it from genesis (GroupEpochs{since: 0}) before applying R2/R5, or must persist the seen-c0 and seen-commit sets alongside its pin and update them on every accepted record; require the 6.4 bundle to carry the complete chain and have 'recovery author' refuse a partial one.
